title: Forward Roll and V-balance
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 3 Creative Activities; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Activities teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Mats or soft grass only. The teacher demonstrates and spots every roll. Markers: bottle tops or bean bags at the start line.

skills.key_step: The child names the body parts used in a forward roll (hands, tucked chin, back of the shoulders, round back) and a V-balance (the bottom, lifted legs and chest).

floor.prerequisite: Performs an egg roll with a tucked body (Grade 2).
floor.question: In an egg roll, is your body tucked or stretched?

steps: Squat with hands flat on the mat.
Roll on the back of the shoulders.
For the V, sit and lift legs and chest.
contexts: a gymnastics display on sports day
a PE lesson on the grass

board.do: Show a picture of a child rolling.
Wait for: tucked to the chest.

misconceptions.ask: In a forward roll, which part touches the mat first after the hands?
misconceptions.repair: Tuck the chin onto a bean bag held at the chest.

misconceptions.ask: What shape is your back in a forward roll?
misconceptions.repair: Rock on the back like a rocking chair first.

misconceptions.ask: In a V-balance, where are your feet?
misconceptions.repair: Lift one leg, then both, holding the knees first.

misconceptions.ask: What part of the body do you balance on in a V-balance?
misconceptions.repair: Sit and lift legs and chest together, arms out.

checks.question: In a forward roll, where is your chin?
In a V-balance, what do you balance on?
